journey.title: Walk the settings tabs with arrow keys
journey.goal: Each arrow press selects and focuses the next tab

functionalJourney.title: Switch settings sections with the mouse
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking a tab shows its panel

guards.title: Tab from the active tab into its panel
guards.goal: Tab leaves the tab list for the active panel

plan.root_cause: The ArrowRight keydown handler in tab.js updates the aria-selected state of the next tab but does not move focus to it, causing focus to remain on the previous tab or the body after the key press.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify the _keydown method in js/src/tab.js to focus the newly activated tab after invoking its show() method, ensuring keyboard navigation moves focus alongside selection.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Arrow key navigation will now move focus to the next tab, making the focused tab match the selected tab and satisfying keyboard operability requirements (WCAG 2.1.1, 2.4.3).
functional_risks: Focusing the tab after show() could interfere if show() already focuses the element in future versions.
If a tab panel contains an autofocus element, moving focus to the tab first may briefly shift focus away from that element, but this is acceptable as the tab is the entry point.
Mouse click behavior remains unchanged because clicking a button already focuses it.
verification_requirements: Pressing ArrowRight from a tab moves focus to the next tab and updates its aria-selected to true.
Pressing ArrowLeft from a tab moves focus to the previous tab and updates its aria-selected to true.
Focus loops correctly from the last tab to the first and vice versa.
Tab panels show/hide correctly when tabs are changed via arrow keys.
Mouse clicks on tabs continue to work as expected.
No JavaScript errors are thrown during keyboard navigation.
